about: FYP: how the TikTok algorithm picks your next video. Meta puzzle film: TikTok bet you'd watch this. Every swipe is a signal (finish, skip, replay, seconds watched; TikTok's own pages), then the twist from TikTok's own example: a stranger who watched the same two videos helps pick your third. Ends asking if you finished this one. Factory #6. Narration-led: the voice is recorded first and every visual beat is keyed to its word times.

lines.text: So how does the TikTok algorithm know?
Every swipe is a clue: finish, skip, or replay.
lines.say: Every swipe is a clue. Finish, skip, or replay.

lines.text: Even the seconds you linger get counted.
Finish a long video? TikTok calls that a strong sign.
But here's the trick. It's not just you.
Say a stranger saw two of the same videos you did.
TikTok may guess you'll like her third one too.
So a stranger you'll never meet helped pick your feed.
In 2021, the New York Times saw TikTok's internal guide.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-one, the New York Times saw TikTok's internal guide.

lines.text: Two numbers mattered: do you come back? How long do you stay?
lines.say: Two numbers mattered. Do you come back? How long do you stay?

lines.text: So, did you finish this one? Yes or no?
